about: Built by web/site/tools/build_catalog.mjs from the FM-1 Firmware Hub's catalog, FM1VST's cores and RemoteFM1's own release (web/installer/releases.json). Edit those, not this file.

fm1emu.name: fm1-emu
fm1emu.author: Joakim Eriksson
fm1emu.line: Emulated by fm1-emu, the FM-1 emulator by Joakim Eriksson (MIT licence): https://github.com/joakimeriksson/fm1-emu

firmwares.name: AMB-1
firmwares.author: C. Vestal
firmwares.what: A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.

firmwares.name: BEETLE
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken
firmwares.what: A tracker for the FM-1: patterns written top to bottom, step by step, with note, instrument, chord and effect columns, the way trackers have always worked.

firmwares.name: Bubba Machine
firmwares.author: Erbubar23
firmwares.what: A six-track groovebox written from scratch: TR drums from Plaits' 808 and 909 models, a sampler with a 16-slice slicer, a bass and three free tracks (analog, 6-op FM, 303 acid), scenes and fills, all at 44.1 kHz.
firmwares.emuNote: boots to a black screen, no sound (needs M-VAVE's own loader)

firmwares.name: ChoralRoot
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.what: A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.

firmwares.name: CoralFlower
firmwares.author: FicusFicusov
firmwares.what: Chords after the Orchid, with a UX made for the FM-1: one key turns every note into a chord with a bass, 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a looper, a plate reverb, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.

firmwares.name: CS-1
firmwares.author: twochannels
firmwares.what: A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.

firmwares.name: CTL-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A MIDI controller: notes in any scale with its chords on the black keys, four banks of knobs, an arpeggiator and Euclidean drums, with General MIDI sounds of its own when nothing is connected.

firmwares.name: Dinghy
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.tag: Your base for your own FM-1…
firmwares.what: Your base for your own FM-1 firmware: everything under it done and documented (updates, USB rescue, USB-MIDI, USB audio, keys, screen, settings), a 4-voice sine on top. Fork it, replace the sine.

firmwares.name: DUELL
firmwares.author: OSCILL/R
firmwares.what: A multimorphing bitimbral synthesizer: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound.

firmwares.name: ETCH
firmwares.author: SikkenWorks
firmwares.what: Draw the sound: a waveform drawn and changed with the knobs, saved, morphed into another one, and a third waveform modulating the result.

firmwares.name: Fart Machine One
firmwares.author: A. C. Wilson
firmwares.what: A questionable musical instrument: eleven artisanal farts, reverb, delay and a sixteen-step sequencer.

firmwares.name: Felucca
firmwares.author: Hügelton
firmwares.what: The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.

firmwares.name: Felucca [Salt]
firmwares.author: Chance Roth
firmwares.what: Felucca with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser (play it there without an FM-1): many engines, presets, skins. A beta.

firmwares.name: Felucca 8 Patterns
firmwares.author: echoe
firmwares.what: Felucca 1.5.1 with eight sequences a track to switch between and chain one after another; the user samples are left out to make room.

firmwares.name: FiMba-1
firmwares.author: J. Sowers
firmwares.what: A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: FM-106
firmwares.author: PatttF
firmwares.what: The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.

firmwares.name: FM1 Quest
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.what: A pixel-art RPG while you make music, built on SLOOP: four heroes, one a track, walk through a village and fight monsters and bosses as your loop plays, every SLOOP screen redrawn in the game's style.

firmwares.name: fm1-chord
firmwares.author: math0ne
firmwares.what: A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.

firmwares.name: FMini-1
firmwares.author: ruppert
firmwares.what: A three-oscillator Minimoog-style monosynth on Felucca 1.6.1, with 100 factory patches.

firmwares.name: FOMAJAM
firmwares.author: konsumer
firmwares.what: A drum machine in the classic step-grid style: voices after the 909, 808, 707, 606, DMX and more, a machine per voice, accents and patterns. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: FoMni
firmwares.author: C. Vestal
firmwares.what: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.

firmwares.name: Frodhes
firmwares.author: L. Mirabal
firmwares.what: A Rhodes electric piano, physically modelled, no samples: four piano types, compressor, drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb, tap tempo, MIDI clock, scales and presets. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: FuMi-1
firmwares.author: cartesive
firmwares.what: A shigin conductor after the Suiko ST-50: its two rows of keys, the key set in honsū, equal or its own just tuning, a koto and twelve more sounds on a 6-op FM engine, ring time, vibrato, trill and a looper.

firmwares.name: GHOULBOX
firmwares.author: J. Persinger
firmwares.what: Dungeon synth: a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.

firmwares.name: GR!MM
firmwares.author: GRiMMBIENT
firmwares.what: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream: four tracks, seven sound sources from VA and 6-op FM to formant voices and physical models, tape, granular freeze and reverbs up to infinite, a 64-step sequencer and song mode. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: Hortator
firmwares.author: DEADACTIVE
firmwares.what: A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: HYP-1
firmwares.author: RedtailWorks
firmwares.what: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1.

firmwares.name: Jangada
firmwares.author: zednaked
firmwares.what: Dark, industrial, Brazilian: drones that breathe, ten engines (6-op FM, a superwave analog with a ladder filter), four tracks, a mod matrix, live effects.

firmwares.name: JIANT FM
firmwares.author: juanjiant
firmwares.what: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.

native.preferredWhy: the Hub's 0.9.9-6968b20 is the same 0.9.9 release, one commit before the 0912abb FM1VST builds, and the native core is far lighter on the CPU

firmwares.name: LOOM-8
firmwares.author: C. Vestal
firmwares.what: A pocket groovebox: eight tracks on nine engines, a 64-step sequencer with locks, weave, scenes and a song, and a user sample bank loaded over USB.

firmwares.name: MAKU
firmwares.author: okumurari
firmwares.what: An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: MC-1
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.what: An original four-part groovebox with a 1990s workflow: three melodic parts and a 16-lane drum part, 128 melodic presets, eight drum kits, song arrangement, an arpeggiator and recorded knob moves.

firmwares.name: Melodee
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.what: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.

firmwares.name: MIN-1
firmwares.author: Reytian
firmwares.what: A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.

firmwares.name: Mini-Tone
firmwares.author: S. Schmitz
firmwares.what: Felucca 1.5 with six tracks and ten engines: SID, CHIP, DUALVCO, ANALOG4, BRAIDS, SWARMER, FMTONE, WAVETONE, FMDRUM and TB303.

firmwares.name: MYCELIUM
firmwares.author: Mandalars
firmwares.what: Forest, Psytrance, Goa and Hitech grooves, built on Felucca and SLOOP: original drums and icons and four factory songs. A test release: not yet fully tested on the device.

firmwares.name: No Man Sky FM
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.what: A space adventure while you make music, built on SLOOP 2.7.1: fly between planets with two knobs, land, mine, fight sentinels and warp between stars, every SLOOP screen floating over the game.

firmwares.name: NOIZ DEMONS
firmwares.author: SPIKE the Percussionist
firmwares.what: Felucca with randomization as a ritual: every new sound summons one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, its sigil takes the screen and its rank decides how wild the sound gets.

firmwares.name: OberVave
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84: two oscillators a voice, sync, cross-mod, a 12 / 24 dB filter with a SEM-style morph, an arpeggiator with hold, chorus, ping-pong delay and a plate reverb. A two-track step sequencer played as sloopDX: live recording on top, chords, long notes, a click and a count-in.

firmwares.name: ORBIT
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.what: A four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine in a colour-coded Synth, Drum, Event Tape and Mixer workflow, loops turned into songs, user macros, screens after the OP-1. Based on SLOOP.
firmwares.nativeGated: OP-1 material and the Hügelton icon atlas

firmwares.name: PIGEON
firmwares.author: The Shrimp Blimp
firmwares.what: An old-school hip-hop and house sampler after the SP-404 and the PO-33: two song samples and a 16-pad kit, up to 32 chops a song, a 64-step sequencer, patterns and a song arrangement. Built on Felucca.

native.preferredWhy: the Hub's newer build is a beta (FM1VST pins PIGEON's latest stable release), and the native core is far lighter on the CPU

firmwares.name: Pocket GammaWave
firmwares.author: ShadowTune
firmwares.what: The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.

firmwares.name: Polly
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.what: A pocket arranger after the QY70: pick a style, play three keys for a chord and a band of eight follows, songs from sections, General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, and a General MIDI module over MIDI in.

firmwares.name: PurpleMonkey
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.what: A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.

firmwares.name: Rainbow Mode
firmwares.author: J. Bartlett
firmwares.what: A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.

firmwares.name: RemoteFM1
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.what: The firmware this site installs, running as itself. It turns an FM-1 into a USB panel for a computer, so it makes no sound of its own: it shows a screen and waits for a host. In a browser tab, no host is coming.
firmwares.blurb: Plays nothing. Waits for a host.

firmwares.name: Shine On
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: A string ensemble in the spirit of the late-70s machines, grown out of OberVave: divide-down keyers with 16', 8' and 4' footages, register filters, a three-tap BBD ensemble and a phaser, on two tracks with the sequencer.

firmwares.name: Skiff
firmwares.author: illuminus5
firmwares.what: Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca 1.1.5; its sounds and projects load.

firmwares.name: SLOOP
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.what: A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.

firmwares.name: SLOOP DX7 Banks
firmwares.author: majnikool
firmwares.what: SLOOP 2.4 with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in the editor, presets by kind. Test builds: back up first.

firmwares.name: SLOOP Floyd FM
firmwares.author: René Bohne
firmwares.what: SLOOP with a visual four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an ADSR per operator, seven pages, a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.

firmwares.name: sloopDX
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.

firmwares.name: Speak37
firmwares.author: M. Geisler
firmwares.what: The talking synth, its FM-1 build: every key speaks the next word of a sentence at its pitch and chords speak in harmony; nine voices, 20 banks of sentences and songs, RHYTHM with an 808.

firmwares.name: Tonitor
firmwares.author: N. Zimas
firmwares.what: Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.
firmwares.license: GPL-3.0-only (+ Apache-2.0 msfa, MIT Rings, BSD-3 LIRA-8)

firmwares.name: TRIBE
firmwares.author: apiel
firmwares.what: A ten-track groovebox where any engine plays on any track: kicks, 909 and 808 voices, the 303, sixteen clips a track, scatter effects and four master knobs you assign. Built on X0X.

firmwares.name: Tuna
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.what: Generative music built on Felucca: composer profiles write the music as it plays, you steer them. A work in progress.

firmwares.name: Vector37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.what: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.

firmwares.name: WaveLoop FM-1
firmwares.author: ELI7VH
firmwares.what: Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: track faders, a DJ filter, momentary effect pads; 32 patches a bank, 12 evolving songs, revoiced 808 and CR78 kits.

firmwares.name: winampFM Synth
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.what: Winamp 2.x on the FM-1, built on SLOOP: your sounds as a playlist, four tracks you record as loops, effects on sliders and a visualizer made of lines. The real firmware plays in a 3D simulator first.

firmwares.name: X0X
firmwares.author: C. Vestal
firmwares.what: A groovebox: 909 and 808 drums, two 303s with TB-3PO, a breakbeat generator and song mode.

firmwares.name: X0X-RMX
firmwares.author: Mr-Roboto
firmwares.what: X0X remixed after The Orb: banks and patterns reordered live per voice, Grids MAP and EUCLID drum generation, an extended TB-3PO with 22 scales and a morphing 303 waveform. Built on X0X.

firmwares.name: zp12
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.what: A standalone 12-bit sampler inspired by the E-mu SP-1200: sample in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), unplug, and the FM-1 plays on its own: nothing smoothed, loops and songs.
